refuted.lead: gpuPresence DETECTS an accelerator and nothing in the tree dispatches to one. The field is honest but the gap is permanent until something uses it
refuted.killed_by: MEASURED, on real hardware, through the browser harness at /os — the first time anything in this repository has run on a GPU. The shader AGREED with the CPU reference element for element at every size, so the dispatch is correct. And the CPU won at every size: 1525.88x at 1,024 elements, 10.39x at 16,384, 4.84x at 262,144 and 2.72x at 1,048,576. The prediction recorded before the measurement was that the CPU would win below roughly a hundred thousand elements; it in fact wins at a million, the margin narrowing but never crossing. A dispatch is a buffer write, a submit and a readback, and that fixed cost never amortises against 37-83 ns/element on work this shape. The dispatch stays as a MEASURED negative result rather than a capability: it is real, it is correct, and it is slower. — CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, and the refutation above measured the wrong arrangement. Those figures are the GPU used ALONE, awaited immediately, which idles the CPU and can only lose. Split across both processors with the dispatch submitted first and the CPU share computed while it is in flight, the involution BEATS the CPU alone at 1,048,576 elements: 170.70 ms for CPU alone against 134.90 ms at a 10% GPU share (1.27x), 141.10 ms at 50% (1.21x) and 159.40 ms at 25% (1.07x), with correctness holding at every split. It loses again at 75% and 100%. The ordering is NON-MONOTONIC, so run-to-run noise is comparable to the effect and no optimal split is claimed — only that the involution can beat either processor alone, which is the opposite of what the first measurement concluded.

refused.developed: 2026-09-01 — THE ARITHMETIC HALF IS NOW MEASURED, which is exactly what the boundary permits keeping. Walked forward (x→2x mod 9, y→y+2 mod 7) against inverse (x→5x mod 9, y→y-2 mod 7) from (1,1): 42 DISTINCT states in 42 steps, return to (1,1) at 42, and the forward and inverse walks coincide at exactly two points — step 21 at (8,1) and step 42 at (1,1). refused.derived: and the TWO is not an observation, it is forced. Forward is (2^n mod 9, 2n mod 7) and inverse is (5^n mod 9, -2n mod 7), so they meet iff 4^n ≡ 1 (mod 9) and 4n ≡ 0 (mod 7). Sealable as closed integer arithmetic: (4^3 % 9 = 1) ∧ (21 = 3*7) ∧ (42 / 21 = 2).

refused.lead: shadcn/ui distributes flat files through a served, schema-d, namespaced catalogue (registry.json + registry-item.json, 12 item types, @namespace/name, ${ENV} auth headers, an MCP door that installs). uuidna generates 255 MCP tools and six @uuidna/* surfaces reachable ONLY by calling its own MCP: no catalogue a downstream can resolve, no namespace under which anyone can pin and fetch a dependency closure. uuidna_registry exists as a TOOL; a registry as a SERVED ARTIFACT does not.
refused.boundary: An INVOLUTION, not a licence clash. shadcn gives the CODE away (MIT, the consumer owns the copy) and KEEPS the catalogue as its product surface; this tree keeps the CODE (CC-BY-NC-ND, no derivative, no commerce) and GIVES the catalogue away (read-only tools, free to call). Those are the two ends of one map. Adopting shadcn-s distribution while holding NC-ND would put this tree at NEITHER end, keeping both the code and the catalogue — the one position the involution has no fixed point for. The licence text is downstream of that, not the cause. Measured: npm shadcn 4.21.0, MIT; shadcn-ui/ui 123069 stars; both schemas fetched and their enums enumerated from the served JSON. NOT CLAIMED: that any downstream has asked for a registry — none has.
